articles.title: The UFC Has Moved On From Jon Jones #ufc
articles.description: Jon Jones says he likes the idea of getting back in there and hurting somebody one more time. But Chael Sonnen believes there's a major problem with that idea: the UFC heavyweight division has moved on. Chael isn't questioning Jones' ability. In fact, that's exactly the problem. He believes Jon is still so dangerous that putting him in a championship fight would make him the overwhelming favorite. If Jones wins, he walks away with the heavyweight title again, leaving the UFC to rebuild a division that has already spent considerable time moving forward. Chael explains why bringing Jon Jones back isn't as simple as finding him an opponent. At this point, he believes there may not be a matchup that makes sense for the UFC or the heavyweight division. #JonJones #UFC #Heavyweight #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews

articles.title: Should the UFC Sign Usman After the Merab Incident? #ufc
articles.description: Should the UFC sign Usman following the incident involving Merab Dvalishvili? Chael Sonnen questions whether the UFC's interest in signing Usman should be affected by what happened. Merab has reportedly said the two are on good terms, that he has forgiven Usman, and that he wants others to do the same. Chael isn't defending what happened. He makes it clear that he believes Usman's actions were wrong. But he also points out that Usman has already faced serious consequences, including time in prison and potentially never being allowed back into the country. Should the UFC add to those consequences, or is it time to let the situation move forward? Chael makes the case that accountability matters, but so does recognizing when someone has already been punished. #UFC #MerabDvalishvili #KamaruUsman #MMA #UFCNews #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Josh Hokit’s Takedown Was Crazy #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen doesn't expect this to be a close fight. In his mind, somebody is going to get dominated, and Josh Hokit's wrestling could determine who. Before Josh fought Derrick Lewis, Chael had one major question: Could Hokit actually get a heavyweight opponent to the ground when he needed to? That question didn't last long. Chael recalls watching Hokit take down Derrick Lewis so quickly that he had to replay the sequence multiple times. Eventually, he realized the takedown was happening too fast for him to even break down what he was seeing. Now, Chael sees that explosive wrestling as a major weapon and believes it could make all the difference in Josh's next matchup. #JoshHokit #DerrickLewis #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #Wrestling If you send the rest of the transcript, I can make sure the package captures the full argument rather than just the takedown setup.

articles.title: Matthew McConaughey Is LYING About His Tuna Salad
articles.description: Chael Sonnen has tried to let this go, but Matthew McConaughey's tuna salad story has finally pushed him too far. McConaughey has shared his unusual tuna recipe on multiple podcasts, complete with wasabi, guava, frozen peas, corn and crushed potato chips. Chael has one problem: he doesn't believe McConaughey has ever actually made it. From the ingredients supposedly sitting in his refrigerator to putting crushed chips into tuna and leaving it overnight, Chael breaks down every part of the story—and explains why Bert Kreischer's reaction might bother him even more than the recipe itself. And somehow, Woody Harrelson gets dragged into this.

articles.title: Jon Jones Does NOT Understand the Fight Business
articles.description: Jon Jones says the idea of coming back and beating someone up one more time sounds appealing. Chael Sonnen believes Jones is missing the reality of his current position. According to Chael, the UFC has already moved on. The heavyweight division has a champion, Jones no longer holds the belt, and simply wanting another fight isn't enough. If Jones truly wants back in, Chael believes he needs to identify an opponent, Ciryl Gane, Tom Aspinall, Alex Pereira, or Josh Hokit and give the UFC a story it can actually sell. More importantly, Chael explains why keeping Jones under contract may be more valuable to the UFC than actually booking him to fight—and why Jones may be misunderstanding the business leverage he still has.

articles.title: What Needs to Be Done With Ciryl Gane's Eye Pokes?
articles.description: Josh Hokit says he's dealing with blurry vision following his fight with Ciryl Gane, and Chael Sonnen believes MMA has reached a point where it needs to decide how seriously it actually takes eye pokes. Chael does not believe Gane is intentionally cheating. But intent doesn't change the fact that fighters are being injured, and the current rules leave referees with very few options when an eye poke is deemed accidental. Using Rousimar Palhares, wrestling's biting rules, bare-knuckle boxing, and other combat sports as comparisons, Chael asks whether MMA needs a real solution or whether eye pokes will become another problem the sport talks about without ever fixing.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria vs. Paddy Pimblett Has Fallen Into the UFC's Lap
articles.description: Ilia Topuria and Paddy Pimblett have now both publicly suggested the same idea: coach The Ultimate Fighter against each other and then fight. Chael Sonnen believes the UFC has been handed an opportunity that's almost impossible to turn down. Paddy proposed the idea weeks ago, and now Topuria has independently called for the exact same thing. With both fighters apparently on board, Chael explains why Topuria vs. Pimblett could be one of the biggest fights the UFC can make and why a season of The Ultimate Fighter could make it even bigger.

articles.title: Dan Hooker: "I Want Max Holloway for the REAL BMF Title"
articles.description: Dan Hooker called out Max Holloway following his latest win, and Chael Sonnen believes the timing couldn't be more interesting. Holloway appears to be waiting on a potential trilogy with Conor McGregor, but Chael sees a major risk in that strategy. Michael Chandler already spent years waiting for McGregor, only to watch the opportunity disappear. With no guarantee McGregor vs. Holloway III ever happens, should Max really put his career on hold? Chael breaks down Hooker's callout, the proposed BMF fight with Holloway, and one contradiction in Hooker's argument about Charles Oliveira that he can't reconcile.

articles.title: Josh Hokit Wants Consequences: "I Have To Poke Him"
articles.description: Josh Hokit walked into Madison Square Garden 10-0 and walked out with his first loss. Ciryl Gane kept the UFC heavyweight title at UFC 334, winning a unanimous decision (48-47 on all three cards) after landing 237 significant strikes, the most ever by one fighter in a UFC heavyweight fight. Hokit landed 146. Somewhere in that war, a Gane finger went into Hokit's eye and no point was taken. After the fight, with his vision still blurry, Hokit took to Instagram with a message for the champion: "There has to be consequences next time." He wants an immediate rematch, and Dana White, who admits he's had his issues with Hokit, came away calling him "the real deal." 0:00 Hokit's warning 0:10 His first loss 0:20 UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit 0:33 Dana White: "He fought the perfect fight" 0:51 Record strikes, the decision and the eye poke 1:13 Dana White: "Unbelievable chin, unstoppable cardio" 1:41 Hokit's Instagram message: "There has to be consequences" 2:28 The rematch push and Dana's verdict Should the UFC run it back right away? articles.title: The Law of the Locker Room #ufc
articles.description: There's an unwritten code in the fight game, and Chael Sonnen is explaining how it works. Chael describes something known as a "receipt." When you do something to another person and they eventually return the favor, the score is settled. In the locker room, the expectation is simple: if you know you deserved it, you accept your receipt, let it go, and move on. But there's another side to that code. According to Chael, the rules of the playground are different. If somebody does something to you and you never respond, people may look at you differently. Chael makes it clear that he didn't create these rules, and he doesn't necessarily agree with them. He's simply explaining the culture and unwritten expectations that exist inside combat sports. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #FightCulture #MMAStories

articles.title: Amanda vs. Kayla BOMBED—Now What?
articles.description: Amanda Nunes vs. Kayla Harrison had everything a major fight should have: a world title, a GOAT debate, history between the fighters, and two separate promotional campaigns. According to Chael Sonnen, the audience still didn't care. Now the UFC has a much bigger problem. Despite the lack of interest in their first fight, Chael can't identify another opponent for Amanda or Kayla that fans would rather see. So what do you do? Run back a fight that already failed to capture the audience—or make an even less interesting matchup in hopes of building something for the future?

articles.title: How the UFC Can Set Up Hokit vs. Pereira #ufc
articles.description: How does the UFC make Josh Hokit vs. Alex Pereira happen? Chael Sonnen believes the answer starts with Alexander Volkov. There are several ways the matchup could come together. If Pereira loses, he could potentially be matched with Hokit. If Pereira wins but doesn't receive the next title shot, that could also open the door. But Chael sees an even better route: give Volkov a shot at the heavyweight championship. That move could help clear the path for Hokit and Pereira to meet, regardless of the outcome of Pereira's fight with Sergei Pavlovich. Chael explains why Volkov getting the title opportunity may be the key to making one of the most exciting heavyweight matchups possible. #UFC #JoshHokit #AlexPereira #AlexanderVolkov #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Israel Adesanya’s Interview Has Me VERY Concerned
articles.description: Israel Adesanya says he stopped using his greatest weapon, his fight IQ, and is now getting back to being “The Stylebender.” Chael Sonnen isn't convinced that's the answer. Chael explains why fighters are often the last people to recognize their own decline, why changing gyms and searching for new answers concerns him, and why no amount of mindset or fight IQ can replace the physical work required to return to the top. Chael remains an Adesanya fan and hopes he's proven wrong. But after hearing Izzy explain his path back, he calls it the most concerning Adesanya interview he's ever seen.

articles.title: Here's How We Get Hokit vs. Pereira
articles.description: Josh Hokit and Alex Pereira have made it clear they want to fight each other. Chael Sonnen believes there's a path to making it happen, and Alexander Volkov may hold the key. Chael breaks down the moving pieces at heavyweight, including Tom Aspinall's absence, Ciryl Gane's next title defense, Pereira's fight with Sergei Pavlovich, and Volkov's increasingly public campaign for a title shot. If Volkov can get Hokit and Pereira occupied with each other, Chael believes his own path to Gane opens up. And Hokit vs. Pereira could become the “people's main event” on the same card.

articles.title: Joe Rogan Is Wrong About Ilia Topuria
articles.description: Joe Rogan believes Ilia Topuria should return to 145 pounds after facing Justin Gaethje at lightweight. Chael Sonnen strongly disagrees. Chael argues that Topuria and Gaethje both weighed exactly 155 pounds, and rejects the idea that Gaethje was simply “too big” for Ilia. He also believes their fight was much closer than people remember and questions why a world champion would cut weight to avoid tougher competition. From Topuria and Gaethje to Jon Jones, Alex Pereira and Josh Hokit, Chael explains why he believes the entire conversation about who is “too big” is fundamentally flawed.

articles.title: Harrison vs Nunes 2 at 145? Nunes Says "Rematch Accepted"
articles.description: Kayla Harrison submitted Amanda Nunes in the fourth round at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. Two days later, Nunes posted "145 Rematch, accepted." Dana White's answer: "Sure. Yeah. I'd do it again." We trace both careers through the MMA Weekly archive: Nunes's run from UFC 200 to the double-champ night against Cris Cyborg, the Peña loss, the rematch and her 2023 retirement; Harrison's two Olympic golds, two PFL titles and her UFC run through Holm, Vieira and Peña. Then the round-by-round numbers from UFC 334, what a rematch at 145 would mean for a division with no champion since 2023, and what the 135 rankings look like if the champ moves up. Should Harrison vs Nunes 2 happen at 145? articles.title: Dana White Turns Down Press Secretary, Then Gives $500K at the White House
articles.description: In less than two weeks, UFC CEO Dana White went from a White House job offer to a half-million-dollar gift on the South Lawn. On November 7, President Trump announced on Truth Social that Dana White had been offered the job of White House press secretary. The next night in Palm Beach, Trump said he was "only kidding" but that "Dana loves the idea." On November 9, Dana stepped up to the briefing room podium, took questions from the press, and turned the job down: "I do not want to be in politics." On November 20, Trump and White hosted a reception honoring the U.S. Marine Band, "The President's Own," on the new White House helipad. The gift started at $200,000. Trump raised it to $500,000 and wrote the new number on the check by hand. White thanked the band for the live music at UFC Freedom 250, and the band celebrated its first-ever Grammy nomination.
